candidates.mechanism: dialysate tracking through patent fallopian tubes
candidates.intervention: create a catheter with directional flow channels that mimic the unidirectional flow of fallopian tubes to prevent backflow and tissue ingrowth
candidates.predicted_effect: maintain catheter patency by preventing tissue migration and fibrin accumulation while allowing continuous drainage
candidates.testable_prediction: in vitro test comparing flow rates and tissue adhesion between standard catheters and fallopian tube-inspired catheter designs under simulated abdominal flow conditions

candidates.mechanism: Dialysate tracking from the peritoneal cavity, passing through bilaterally patent fallopian tubes into both the endometrial and vaginal cavities
candidates.intervention: Design a catheter with a directional mesh barrier that mimics the selective permeability of fallopian tube tissue, allowing dialysate to exit but preventing tissue ingrowth
candidates.predicted_effect: Block omental tissue migration into the catheter lumen while maintaining adequate drainage flow
candidates.testable_prediction: Animal study comparing catheter patency between standard catheters and fallopian tube-inspired mesh barriers after prolonged use in low-flow conditions

candidates.mechanism: dialysate tracking from the peritoneal cavity, passing through bilaterally patent fallopian tubes into both the endometrial and vaginal cavities
candidates.intervention: incorporate a one-way valve system within the catheter that allows fluid to exit the catheter but prevents backflow into the peritoneal cavity, mimicking the patent fallopian tube mechanism
candidates.predicted_effect: prevent omental wrapping and fibrin clogging by ensuring unidirectional flow and reducing stagnant conditions that lead to obstruction
candidates.testable_prediction: compare catheter drainage rates in a laboratory simulation with and without the one-way valve under low-flow conditions using a synthetic dialysate containing fibrinogen

candidates.mechanism: fluid tracking through patent fallopian tubes from peritoneal cavity to vaginal cavity
candidates.intervention: create catheter with microfluidic channels that guide fluid flow along specific pathways to prevent random accumulation
candidates.predicted_effect: reduced fibrin clogging by controlling dialysate flow patterns and preventing stagnation points
candidates.testable_prediction: compare drainage rates and fibrin accumulation in catheters with and without microfluidic channels under simulated low abdominal-flow conditions

candidates.mechanism: patent fallopian tubes allowing dialysate to pass from the peritoneal cavity into the vaginal cavity
candidates.intervention: create a micro-perforated catheter sleeve that allows controlled dialysate leakage into the peritoneal cavity around the catheter
candidates.predicted_effect: reduce catheter obstruction by preventing omental wrapping and fibrin clogging through controlled pressure equalization
candidates.testable_prediction: compare catheter patency between standard catheters and modified catheters with micro-perforations in an animal model under low-flow conditions
